sanskrit: rājñām upāyāś catvāro buddhimantraḥ parākramaḥ nigrahānugrahau caiva dākṣyaṃ tatkāryasādhanam
english: A king has four instruments at his disposal: wise counsel, valor, the power to punish and reward, and skill in accomplishing the task at hand.

sanskrit: sāmnā dānena bhedena daṇḍenopekṣaṇena ca sādhanīyāni kāryāṇi samāsavyāsayogataḥ
english: Affairs are to be accomplished through conciliation, gifts, division of enemies, punishment, and disregard — whether by brief or extended application of these means.

sanskrit: mantramūlā nayāḥ sarve cārāś ca bharatarṣabha sumantritair nayaiḥ siddhis tadvidaiḥ saha mantrayet
english: All statecraft and espionage are rooted in counsel, O bull of the Bhāratas. Success comes through well-deliberated policy; one should take counsel together with those who know these arts.

sanskrit: striyā mūḍhena lubdhena bālena laghunā tathā na mantrayeta guhyāni yeṣu conmādalakṣaṇam
english: One should not share secrets with a woman, a fool, a greedy man, a child, or a frivolous person, nor with those who show signs of madness.

sanskrit: mantrayet saha vidvadbhiḥ śaktaiḥ karmāṇi kārayet snigdhaiś ca nītivinyāsān mūrkhān sarvatra varjayet
english: One should deliberate with the learned; have tasks executed by the capable; entrust the arrangements of policy to loyal men; and everywhere shun the foolish.

sanskrit: dhārmikān dharmakāryeṣu arthakāryeṣu paṇḍitān strīṣu klībān niyuñjīta krūrān krūreṣu karmasu
english: In matters of righteousness, employ the righteous; in matters of wealth, employ the wise; in matters concerning women, employ eunuchs; and in cruel tasks, employ the cruel.

sanskrit: svebhyaś caiva parebhyaś ca kāryākāryasamudbhavā buddhiḥ karmasu vijñeyā ripūṇāṃ ca balābalam
english: The intelligence that discerns what must and must not be done — from one's own people and from the enemy — and the measure of the enemy's strength and weakness must be known in all affairs.

sanskrit: buddhyā supratipanneṣu kuryāt sādhuparigraham nigrahaṃ cāpy aśiṣṭeṣu nirmaryādeṣu kārayet
english: Toward those who conduct themselves well according to sound judgment, one should extend favor and acceptance; toward the ill-behaved and the lawless, one should apply restraint.

sanskrit: nigrahe pragrahe samyag yadā rājā pravartate tadā bhavati lokasya maryādā suvyavasthitā
english: When a king rightly applies both restraint and reward, the boundaries of social order become well established for all people.

sanskrit: eṣa te vihitaḥ pārtha ghoro dharmo duranvayaḥ taṃ svadharmavibhāgena vinayastho 'nupālaya
english: This, O Pārtha, is the stern and difficult dharma prescribed for you. Abiding in discipline, maintain it according to the divisions proper to your own duty.

sanskrit: tapodharmadamejyābhir viprā yānti yathā divam dānātithyakriyādharmair yānti vaiśyāś ca sadgatim
english: Just as brahmins reach heaven through austerity, righteousness, self-restraint, and sacrifice, so vaishyas attain the good state through the dharma of giving, hospitality, and proper action.

sanskrit: kṣatraṃ yāti tathā svargaṃ bhuvi nigrahapālanaiḥ samyak praṇīya daṇḍaṃ hi kāmadveṣavivarjitāḥ alubdhā vigatakrodhāḥ satāṃ yānti salokatām
english: So too the kshatriya attains heaven on earth through restraint and protection; wielding the rod of punishment rightly, free from desire and hatred, ungreedy and rid of anger, they reach the world of the righteous.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ saṃhṛtya vipulaṃ tad vapuḥ kāmavardhitam bhīmasenaṃ punar dorbhyāṃ paryaṣvajata vānaraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the monkey, drawing back in that vast body swollen by desire, embraced Bhīmasena once again with his arms.

sanskrit: pariṣvaktasya tasyāśu bhrātrā bhīmasya bhārata śramo nāśam upāgacchat sarvaṃ cāsīt pradakṣiṇam
english: As Bhīma was embraced by his brother, O Bhārata, his fatigue vanished at once and all auspicious signs attended him.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar athovāca paryaśrunayano hariḥ bhīmam ābhāṣya sauhārdād bāṣpagadgadayā girā
english: Then the monkey spoke again, his eyes brimming with tears, addressing Bhīma out of affection with a voice choked with weeping.

sanskrit: gaccha vīra svam āvāsaṃ smartavyo 'smi kathāntare ihasthaś ca kuruśreṣṭha na nivedyo 'smi kasya cit
english: "Go, hero, to your own dwelling. Remember me when the time comes for stories; yet while I dwell here, O best of Kurus, you must not reveal my presence to anyone."

sanskrit: dhanadasyālayāc cāpi visṛṣṭānāṃ mahābala deśakāla ihāyātuṃ devagandharvayoṣitām
english: "For the divine women of the gandharvas, released from the abode of Kubera, the lord of wealth, will come here at the right place and time, O great-armed one."

sanskrit: mamāpi saphalaṃ cakṣuḥ smāritaś cāsmi rāghavam mānuṣaṃ gātrasaṃsparśaṃ gatvā bhīma tvayā saha
english: "My sight too has borne fruit, and I have been reminded of Rāma of the Raghu line. Having obtained the touch of a human body by meeting you, Bhīma, it has been worthwhile."

sanskrit: tad asmaddarśanaṃ vīra kaunteyāmogham astu te bhrātṛtvaṃ tvaṃ puraskṛtya varaṃ varaya bhārata
english: "So let this meeting of ours not be in vain for you, O hero, son of Kuntī. Placing our brotherhood foremost, ask a boon, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: yadi tāvan mayā kṣudrā gatvā vāraṇasāhvayam dhārtarāṣṭrā nihantavyā yāvad etat karomy aham
english: "If those wretched sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra are to be slain by me when I go to Hāstinapura, I shall do it now, as much as you wish."

sanskrit: śilayā nagaraṃ vā tan marditavyaṃ mayā yadi yāvad adya karomy etat kāmaṃ tava mahābala
english: "Or if that city must be crushed by me with a boulder, I shall do it today, as much as your desire requires, O great-armed one."

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu tad vākyaṃ śrutvā tasya mahātmanaḥ pratyuvāca hanūmantaṃ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā
english: Bhīmasena, hearing those words of the great-souled one, replied to Hanūmān with his heart overflowing with joy.

sanskrit: kṛtam eva tvayā sarvaṃ mama vānarapuṃgava svasti te 'stu mahābāho kṣāmaye tvāṃ prasīda me
english: "All has already been done by you for me, O bull among monkeys. May well-being be yours, O great-armed one. I ask your forgiveness — be gracious to me."

sanskrit: sanāthāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ sarve tvayā nāthena vīryavan tavaiva tejasā sarvān vijeṣyāmo vayaṃ ripūn
english: "All the Pāṇḍavas are protected, having you as our protector, O valiant one. By your very radiance we shall conquer all our enemies."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu hanumān bhīmasenam abhāṣata bhrātṛtvāt sauhṛdāc cāpi kariṣyāmi tava priyam
english: Thus addressed, Hanūmān spoke to Bhīmasena: "Out of brotherhood and affection I shall do what is dear to you."

sanskrit: camūṃ vigāhya śatrūṇāṃ śaraśaktisamākulām yadā siṃharavaṃ vīra kariṣyasi mahābala tadāhaṃ bṛṃhayiṣyāmi svaraveṇa ravaṃ tava
english: "When you plunge into the enemy's army thick with arrows and javelins, O hero, and let forth your lion-roar, O great-armed one, then I shall amplify your cry with my own voice."

sanskrit: vijayasya dhvajasthaś ca nādān mokṣyāmi dāruṇān śatrūṇāṃ te prāṇaharān ity uktvāntaradhīyata
english: "Standing on Arjuna's banner, I shall release terrifying cries that will take the lives of your enemies." Saying this, he disappeared.

sanskrit: gate tasmin harivare bhīmo 'pi balināṃ varaḥ tena mārgeṇa vipulaṃ vyacarad gandhamādanam
english: After that foremost of monkeys had departed, Bhīma too, the best among the strong, roamed widely over the Gandhamādana by the path he had come.

sanskrit: anusmaran vapus tasya śriyaṃ cāpratimāṃ bhuvi māhātmyam anubhāvaṃ ca smaran dāśarather yayau
english: Recalling Hanūmān's form and his matchless splendor on earth, remembering the greatness and power of the son of Daśaratha, he went his way.

sanskrit: sa tāni ramaṇīyāni vanāny upavanāni ca viloḍayām āsa tadā saugandhikavanepsayā
english: He then searched through those delightful forests and groves, eager to find the grove of saugandhika flowers.

sanskrit: phullapadmavicitrāṇi puṣpitāni vanāni ca mattavāraṇayūthāni paṅkaklinnāni bhārata varṣatām iva meghānāṃ vṛndāni dadṛśe tadā
english: He then saw forests rich with blooming lotuses, flowering woodlands, herds of rutting elephants mired in mud, and clouds gathered as if ready to pour rain, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: hariṇaiś cañcalāpāṅgair hariṇīsahitair vane saśaṣpakavalaiḥ śrīmān pathi dṛṣṭo drutaṃ yayau
english: Seen on the path by deer with darting eyes accompanied by their does, chewing mouthfuls of young grass, the glorious one passed quickly on.

sanskrit: mahiṣaiś ca varāhaiś ca śārdūlaiś ca niṣevitam vyapetabhīr giriṃ śauryād bhīmaseno vyagāhata
english: Bhīmasena, fearless through his valor, plunged into the mountain frequented by buffaloes, wild boars, and tigers.

sanskrit: kusumānataśākhaiś ca tāmprapallavakomalaiḥ yācyamāna ivāraṇye drumair mārutakampitaiḥ
english: He passed through the forest past trees with flower-laden branches, their tender copper-colored shoots soft, the trees swaying in the wind as if beseeching him.

sanskrit: kṛtapadmāñjalipuṭā mattaṣaṭpadasevitāḥ priyatīrthavanā mārge padminīḥ samatikraman
english: On the path he passed lotus ponds with cupped blossoms like folded palms, attended by intoxicated bees, their forests and sacred fords beloved.

sanskrit: sajjamānamanodṛṣṭiḥ phulleṣu girisānuṣu draupadīvākyapātheyo bhīmaḥ śīghrataraṃ yayau
english: His mind and gaze riveted on the flowering mountain slopes, sustained by the words of Draupadī as his provisions, Bhīma went yet more swiftly.

sanskrit: parivṛtte 'hani tataḥ prakīrṇahariṇe vane kāñcanair vimalaiḥ padmair dadarśa vipulāṃ nadīm
english: Then, as the day turned and deer scattered through the forest, he beheld a vast river adorned with pure golden lotuses.

sanskrit: mattakāraṇḍavayutāṃ cakravākopaśobhitām racitām iva tasyādrer mālāṃ vimalapaṅkajām
english: The river was filled with drunken karandava ducks, beautified by chakravaka birds, and seemed like a garland of pure lotuses fashioned for that mountain.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ nadyāṃ mahāsattvaḥ saugandhikavanaṃ mahat apaśyat prītijananaṃ bālārkasadṛśadyuti
english: In that river the great-souled one beheld a vast grove of saugandhika lotuses, gladdening to behold, radiant as the morning sun.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā labdhakāmaḥ sa manasā pāṇḍunandanaḥ vanavāsaparikliṣṭāṃ jagāma manasā priyām
english: Seeing it and thus having his heart's desire, the son of Pāṇḍu went in thought to his beloved, worn by the hardships of forest exile.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa gatvā nalinīṃ ramyāṃ rākṣasair abhirakṣitām kailāsaśikhare ramye dadarśa śubhakānane
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Going to that lovely lotus-lake guarded by rakshasas on the beautiful peak of Kailāsa, he saw it in a fair and auspicious grove.

sanskrit: kuberabhavanābhyāśe jātāṃ parvatanirjhare suramyāṃ vipulacchāyāṃ nānādrumalatāvṛtām
english: Born near the dwelling of Kubera, fed by mountain torrents, most beautiful, broad-shaded, entwined with many trees and creepers.

sanskrit: haritāmbujasaṃchannāṃ divyāṃ kanakapuṣkarām pavitrabhūtāṃ lokasya śubhām adbhutadarśanām
english: Covered with green lotuses, divine, bearing golden water-lilies, purifying to the world, auspicious and wondrous to behold.

sanskrit: tatrāmṛtarasaṃ śītaṃ laghu kuntīsutaḥ śubham dadarśa vimalaṃ toyaṃ śivaṃ bahu ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: There the son of Kuntī, the Pāṇḍava, beheld the water — cool, light, auspicious, pure, wholesome, and abundant, like the essence of nectar.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu puṣkariṇīṃ ramyāṃ padmasaugandhikāyutām jātarūpamayaiḥ padmaiś channāṃ paramagandhibhiḥ
english: That lovely pond was filled with saugandhika lotuses, covered with blooms of purest gold, supremely fragrant.

sanskrit: vaiḍūryavaranālaiś ca bahucitrair manoharaiḥ haṃsakāraṇḍavoddhūtaiḥ sṛjadbhir amalaṃ rajaḥ
english: With stalks of finest lapis lazuli, many-hued and heart-ravishing, disturbed by swans and karandava ducks that scattered spotless pollen.

sanskrit: ākrīḍaṃ yakṣarājasya kuberasya mahātmanaḥ gandharvair apsarobhiś ca devaiś ca paramārcitām
english: It was the pleasure-ground of the great-souled king of yakshas, Kubera, and was most highly honored by gandharvas, apsarases, and gods.

sanskrit: sevitām ṛṣibhir divyāṃ yakṣaiḥ kiṃpuruṣais tathā rākṣasaiḥ kiṃnaraiś caiva guptāṃ vaiśravaṇena ca
english: It was frequented by divine sages, by yakshas, kimpurushas, rakshasas, and kinnaras, and was guarded by Vaiśravaṇa.

sanskrit: tāṃ ca dṛṣṭvaiva kaunteyo bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ babhūva paramaprīto divyaṃ saṃprekṣya tat saraḥ
english: Beholding that lake, the son of Kuntī, Bhīmasena of great strength, was supremely delighted upon seeing that divine pond.

sanskrit: tac ca krodhavaśā nāma rākṣasā rājaśāsanāt rakṣanti śatasāhasrāś citrāyudhaparicchadāḥ
english: That lake was guarded by a hundred thousand rakshasas called the Krodhavaśa, by order of the king, armed and equipped with diverse weapons.

sanskrit: te tu dṛṣṭvaiva kaunteyam ajinaiḥ parivāritam rukmāṅgadadharaṃ vīraṃ bhīmaṃ bhīmaparākramam
english: They, upon seeing the son of Kuntī clad in deerskins, wearing golden armlets, the hero Bhīma of terrible prowess —

sanskrit: sāyudhaṃ baddhanistriṃśam aśaṅkitam ariṃdamam puṣkarepsum upāyāntam anyonyam abhicukruśuḥ
english: — bearing weapons, his sword girt, the tamer of foes, approaching fearlessly in his desire to reach the lotuses — they cried out to one another.

sanskrit: ayaṃ puruṣaśārdūlaḥ sāyudho 'jinasaṃvṛtaḥ yac cikīrṣur iha prāptas tat saṃpraṣṭum ihārhatha
english: "This tiger among men, bearing weapons and covered in deerskins, has come here with some intention — you ought to ask him what it is."

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve mahābāhuṃ samāsādya vṛkodaram tejoyuktam apṛcchanta kas tvam ākhyātum arhasi
english: Then they all approached that great-armed Vṛkodara, radiant with energy, and asked: "Who are you? You should declare yourself."

sanskrit: muniveṣadharaś cāsi cīravāsāś ca lakṣyase yadartham asi saṃprāptas tad ācakṣva mahādyute
english: "You appear to be wearing the garb of a sage, clothed in bark-cloth. Tell us, O greatly resplendent one, what purpose has brought you here."

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca pāṇḍavo bhīmaseno 'haṃ dharmaputrād anantaraḥ viśālāṃ badarīṃ prāpto bhrātṛbhiḥ saha rākṣasāḥ
english: Bhīma said: "I am Bhīmasena, a Pāṇḍava, next in rank after the son of Dharma; I have come to vast Badarī together with my brothers, O rakshasas."

sanskrit: apaśyat tatra pañcālī saugandhikam anuttamam aniloḍham ito nūnaṃ sā bahūni parīpsati
english: "There the Pāñcālī princess saw an incomparable saugandhika lotus, clearly carried here by the wind; she desires many more of them."

sanskrit: tasyā mām anavadyāṅgyā dharmapatnyāḥ priye sthitam puṣpāhāram iha prāptaṃ nibodhata niśācarāḥ
english: "I have come here to gather a bouquet of flowers for her sake — she of flawless limbs, my beloved, the lawfully wedded wife. Know this, O night-wanderers."

sanskrit: rākṣasā ūcuḥ ākrīḍo 'yaṃ kuberasya dayitaḥ puruṣarṣabha neha śakyaṃ manuṣyeṇa vihartuṃ martyadharmiṇā
english: The rakshasas said: "This is the beloved pleasure-ground of Kubera, O bull among men. No mortal man subject to the law of death may sport here."

sanskrit: devarṣayas tathā yakṣā devāś cātra vṛkodara āmantrya yakṣapravaraṃ pibanti viharanti ca gandharvāpsarasaś caiva viharanty atra pāṇḍava
english: "Divine sages, yakshas, and gods, O Vṛkodara, drink and sport here after taking leave of the great yaksha lord; gandharvas and apsarases too sport here, O Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: anyāyeneha yaḥ kaś cid avamanya dhaneśvaram vihartum icched durvṛttaḥ sa vinaśyed asaṃśayam
english: "Whoever, wrongly and without reverence for the lord of wealth, desires to sport here out of wicked conduct — that one shall surely perish without doubt."

sanskrit: tam anādṛtya padmāni jihīrṣasi balād itaḥ dharmarājasya cātmānaṃ bravīṣi bhrātaraṃ katham
english: "Disregarding him, you wish to take the lotuses from here by force — how then do you call yourself the brother of the king of righteousness?"

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca rākṣasās taṃ na paśyāmi dhaneśvaram ihāntike dṛṣṭvāpi ca mahārājaṃ nāhaṃ yācitum utsahe
english: Bhīma said: "O rakshasas, I do not see the lord of wealth anywhere nearby; and even if I were to see the great king, I would not presume to beg from him."

sanskrit: na hi yācanti rājāna eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ na cāhaṃ hātum icchāmi kṣātradharmaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: "For kings do not beg — that is the eternal law. Nor do I wish to abandon the dharma of the kshatriya under any circumstances."

sanskrit: iyaṃ ca nalinī ramyā jātā parvatanirjhare neyaṃ bhavanam āsādya kuberasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "Moreover, this lovely lotus-pond was born from a mountain stream; it has not reached the dwelling of the great-souled Kubera and thus does not belong to him exclusively."

sanskrit: tulyā hi sarvabhūtānām iyaṃ vaiśravaṇasya ca evaṃgateṣu dravyeṣu kaḥ kaṃ yācitum arhati
english: "This belongs equally to all beings and to Vaiśravaṇa alike. When things stand thus in common, who has the right to beg from whom?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā rākṣasān sarvān bhīmaseno vyagāhata tataḥ sa rākṣasair vācā pratiṣiddhaḥ pratāpavān mā maivam iti sakrodhair bhartsayadbhiḥ samantataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to all the rakshasas, Bhīmasena plunged in. Then the mighty one was stopped by the rakshasas with words — "No! Not like this!" — threatening him angrily on all sides.

sanskrit: kadarthīkṛtya tu sa tān rākṣasān bhīmavikramaḥ vyagāhata mahātejās te taṃ sarve nyavārayan
english: But that one of terrible prowess, treating those rakshasas with contempt, plunged forward; the great-souled one pressed in, and they all tried to stop him.

sanskrit: gṛhṇīta badhnīta nikṛntatemaṃ; pacāma khādāma ca bhīmasenam kruddhā bruvanto 'nuyayur drutaṃ te; śastrāṇi codyamya vivṛttanetrāḥ
english: "Seize him! Bind him! Hack him down! Let us cook and eat Bhīmasena!" — crying out in rage, they swiftly pursued him, brandishing their weapons with rolling eyes.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa gurvīṃ yamadaṇḍakalpāṃ; mahāgadāṃ kāñcanapaṭṭanaddhām pragṛhya tān abhyapatat tarasvī; tato 'bravīt tiṣṭhata tiṣṭhateti
english: Then, seizing his massive mace riveted with bands of gold, dreadful as the rod of Yama, he charged at them swiftly, crying out: "Stand! Stand your ground!"

sanskrit: te taṃ tadā tomarapaṭṭiśādyair; vyāvidhya śastraiḥ sahasābhipetuḥ jighāṃsavaḥ krodhavaśāḥ subhīmā; bhīmaṃ samantāt parivavrur ugrāḥ
english: They then hurled their weapons — darts, iron clubs and the rest — and charged him suddenly, those formidable rakshasas, the Krodhavaśa, consumed by wrath, fierce, surrounding Bhīma on all sides.

sanskrit: vātena kuntyāṃ balavān sa jātaḥ; śūras tarasvī dviṣatāṃ nihantā satye ca dharme ca rataḥ sadaiva; parākrame śatrubhir apradhṛṣyaḥ
english: He who was born powerfully of Kuntī by the Wind, a hero, swift, slayer of enemies, ever devoted to truth and righteousness, unconquerable by foes in valor —

sanskrit: teṣāṃ sa mārgān vividhān mahātmā; nihatya śastrāṇi ca śātravāṇām yathāpravīrān nijaghāna vīraḥ; paraḥśatān puṣkariṇīsamīpe
english: — that great-souled hero cut off their various approaches, shattered the weapons of the enemy, and slew them as they led their charge — more than a hundred — near the lotus-lake.

sanskrit: te tasya vīryaṃ ca balaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā; vidyābalaṃ bāhubalaṃ tathaiva aśaknuvantaḥ sahitāḥ samantād; dhatapravīrāḥ sahasā nivṛttāḥ
english: Seeing his valor and strength, his knowledge-power and the power of his arms alike, unable to withstand him together from all sides, their foremost warriors struck down, they suddenly turned back.

sanskrit: vidīryamāṇās tata eva tūrṇam; ākāśam āsthāya vimūḍhasaṃjñāḥ kailāsaśṛṅgāṇy abhidudruvus te; bhīmārditāḥ krodhavaśāḥ prabhagnāḥ
english: Being shattered right there, swiftly taking to the sky with their senses bewildered, the Krodhavaśa, broken and tormented by Bhīma, fled toward the peaks of Kailāsa.

sanskrit: sa śakravad dānavadaityasaṃghān; vikramya jitvā ca raṇe 'risaṃghān vigāhya tāṃ puṣkariṇīṃ jitāriḥ; kāmāya jagrāha tato 'mbujāni
english: Like Indra overcoming hosts of danavas and daityas, he stepped forth and conquered those troops of enemies in battle; plunging into that lotus-pond, his foes vanquished, he then gathered the lotus-blooms to his heart's content.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa pītvāmṛtakalpam ambho; bhūyo babhūvottamavīryatejāḥ utpāṭya jagrāha tato 'mbujāni; saugandhikāny uttamagandhavanti
english: Then, drinking the nectar-like water, he became renewed in the highest vigor and energy; uprooting and gathering the saugandhika lotuses, supremely fragrant, he took them all.

sanskrit: tatas tu te krodhavaśāḥ sametya; dhaneśvaraṃ bhīmabalapraṇunnāḥ bhīmasya vīryaṃ ca balaṃ ca saṃkhye; yathāvad ācakhyur atīva dīnāḥ
english: Then those Krodhavaśa, driven back by Bhīma's might, gathered themselves and went to the lord of wealth; exceedingly distressed, they reported faithfully Bhīma's valor and strength in battle.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vacas tat tu niśamya devaḥ; prahasya rakṣāṃśi tato 'bhyuvāca gṛhṇātu bhīmo jalajāni kāmaṃ; kṛṣṇānimittaṃ viditaṃ mamaitat
english: Hearing their words, the divine lord laughed and then addressed the rakshasas: "Let Bhīma take the water-born flowers as he pleases; I already know it is for Kṛṣṇā's sake."

sanskrit: tato 'bhyanujñāya dhaneśvaraṃ te; jagmuḥ kurūṇāṃ pravaraṃ viroṣāḥ bhīmaṃ ca tasyāṃ dadṛśur nalinyāṃ; yathopajoṣaṃ viharantam ekam
english: Then, having taken leave of the lord of wealth, they went, their anger gone, to the best of the Kurus, and beheld Bhīma sporting alone in that lotus-lake as he pleased.
